title: Fake News on Social Media
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. Some of this news is true, but some of it is fake. Fake news can look very real because it has photos and strong titles.

Last week, Maria shared a post that said a famous singer was sick. The post was not true. Her friend Ana checked the website and found no news about it.

questions.text: Where do many people read news every day?

options: A post about a singer being sick

questions.text: Why did Ana check the website?
options: She wanted to see if the post was true
She wanted to buy a ticket
She wanted to sing a song

questions.text: What can the reader conclude from the story?
options: It is a good idea to check information before sharing it
Posts on social media are always true
Friends should never talk about the news

vocabulary.definition: the names given to articles or posts
looked at something to make sure it is correct
a message or picture shared online

paragraph_translations: Muitas pessoas leem notícias nas redes sociais todos os dias. Algumas dessas notícias são verdadeiras, mas algumas são falsas. Notícias falsas podem parecer muito reais porque têm fotos e títulos chamativos.

Na semana passada, a Maria compartilhou uma publicação que dizia que um cantor famoso estava doente. A publicação não era verdadeira. A amiga dela, Ana, verificou o site e não encontrou nenhuma notícia sobre isso.
